discussionThreads.author: atelierzoe
discussionThreads.reason: New reply #3539437; expanded public chains verified. Participant-reported score, not independently reproduced or a verified leaderboard movement.
discussionThreads.summary: At October 16 00:04:15 UTC, mikelou1 reports 40%, says the program has no time for an NVARC ensemble, and attributes the shortfall from a 60% cross-validation projection to a small kernel issue. It responds to Adarsh’s doubts about earlier Qwen claims. Both nested chains were expanded in Chrome and without login. Earlier 36% and projected roughly 50% were previous statements; 60% is a projection, not a competition result. Model variant and reproducible method remain undisclosed here.
discussionThreads.title: Qwen3.8-27B / Flash-Next: ARC-AGI-2 results within Kaggle’s compute limits?

discussionThreads.author: anlthms
discussionThreads.reason: Earlier lead re-read without login; body and visible replies publicly accessible. Preserve attribution and distinguish participant results from predictions.
discussionThreads.summary: Anil Thomas posts a prediction that nvbanana is likely to win and attributes his underlying data to huikang’s historical ARC-2 leaderboard page. CPMP replies that he does not know whether they will win, but their submissions have run fast so far. The prediction and response are contestant statements, not an organizer decision, verified winning forecast or disclosed current recipe. Exact root and reply times come from source tooltips.
discussionThreads.title: Pareto front says nvbanana is likely to win

discussionThreads.author: dmitriigluzdov
discussionThreads.reason: Earlier lead re-read without login; body and visible replies publicly accessible. Preserve attribution and distinguish participant results from predictions.
discussionThreads.summary: Dmitrii Gluzdov reports synthetic ARC-rule fine-tuning improves performance on unseen generated rules but has not shown a leaderboard gain. The current post describes 1,369 executable rules and 41,070 generated puzzles, two training approaches, and reported public scores of 30.83 for base NVARC, 29.03 for early LoRA, 27.92 for full LoRA and 29.17 for added blocks. He reports rerun variation of roughly two to four points. Training only on the hard-example file remains untried. These are the author’s experiments and noise estimate; augmented examples are not independent puzzles.
discussionThreads.title: Tried fine-tuning NVARC on new synthetic ARC tasks

discussionThreads.author: darrenamadeusmartin
discussionThreads.reason: Substantive source read and original replies checked; distinguish participant claims from organizer decisions. Logged-out access confirmed.
discussionThreads.summary: Darren Amadeus Martin proposes a deadline extension or GPU change because of grading delays. CPMP argues that a late GPU change would be unfair to teams that spent months tuning for 4xL4. The author replies that fixing the queue is preferable if possible and describes the hardware change as a contingent proposal. No organizer approval was seen.
discussionThreads.title: Petition to delay the end of competition and compute change

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize places Argon behind Astra’s 99.9% ARC-AGI-3 result. It reports 62% fewer actions than the human baseline on the 25 public games, matching or beating three speedrun records and coming within 10% on six others.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Keep the public-demo action comparison separate from the semi-private Verified score.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize says API issues prevented complete standard-harness testing: low reasoning completed 42/55 games for 49.8%; medium completed 46/55 for 46.3%; high completed 19/55 and no score was published. Reported scores retain partial credit across all 55 games. Provider adapter preserves opaque reasoning and permits automatic compaction; standard harness carries notes between turns. Costs use introductory $2 input/$10 output per million tokens.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Material limit on harness comparisons. Do not present incomplete standard-harness runs as a clean capability ceiling.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announces Gemini 4 Argon Verified results: ARC-AGI-3 97.5% at $4.8K with the provider adapter and 49.8% at $5.8K with the standard harness; ARC-AGI-2 91.3% at $0.32/task and ARC-AGI-1 98.5% at $0.16/task. It calls Google DeepMind the second frontier lab above 95% on ARC-AGI-3.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Consequential organizer result. Separate from Kaggle standings. Standard-harness API incompletion is essential context; primary results introduction says 91.2% on v2 while its table and announcement say 91.3%.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announced a new 2026 ARC-AGI-2 Kaggle high of 88.06% by Tufa Labs and said a $150,000 bonus would be split among teams scoring above 85%.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A public-board threshold announcement and major standings lead; the post does not establish a final private score.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Knoop argues experiment ideation is the current bottleneck in recursive self-improvement. He claims coding and execution are largely automated, distinguishes reproducing known results from asking novel questions, and says domain-specific improvement recipes still need human-AI collaboration to spread across domains without further generalization breakthroughs.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Useful organizer perspective on open-ended evaluation and ARC-AGI. His automation percentages and 12-month scenario are attributed claims, not independently verified results.

socialPosts.author: fchollet
socialPosts.summary: Chollet says Argon has a similar ARC-AGI-3 performance profile to Astra and calls Google back at the frontier, quoting ARC Prize’s result.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Attributed organizer reaction to the Verified release; not a separate evaluation.

socialPosts.author: iiiiitsu_ne
socialPosts.summary: Itsu reports moving to rank 30 on Kaggle. The original post links ARC Prize 2026 - ARC-AGI-2.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Dated competitor statement. Later collector snapshot at 20:48:28Z lists Odd Dice, team 16297545, roster nisshokuitsuki, at rank 32; the post is not a current-rank claim.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Knoop calls Argon the second model family effectively to max out ARC-AGI-3 with a provider adapter and notes a similar backwards bend in action efficiency.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Attributed reaction; preserve the provider-adapter qualification and avoid equating it with Kaggle performance.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize links the Verified leaderboard, reproducible public benchmark code, testing policy and full Gemini 4 Argon results.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Primary evidence links for edition follow-up; no new Kaggle ranking.

socialPosts.author: harshitj__
socialPosts.summary: Joshi introduces SHELDON, a reasoning harness that separately tracks hypotheses and observations. His thread claims ARC-AGI-2 improvement over its baselines. The linked Stanford project table reports 59.17 for SHELDON versus 47.50 for EvoX, using GPT-5.6-terra high reasoning and GPT-5.6-luna for delegated implementation.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Fresh primary research lead. These are author-reported experimental results, not Kaggle standings or an ARC Prize Verified evaluation; confirm split, budget and comparability before publication.

socialPosts.author: masspeakss
socialPosts.summary: Translation of Japanese original: An ARC2 merge invitation involving the gold range has come in, so I am torn, but I want to keep trying solo until the last possible moment. The post does not name the inviting team or announce an accepted merger.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Contender motivation and possible future team change; do not report a merger or a verified gold position. Exact current team mapping remains unresolved.
